chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

The example of salat among you is like that of a flowing stream—and it is a river—at the door of one of you; he goes out to it in the day and night and washes in it five times. So no filth remains with washing five times, and no sins remain with salat five times.

key_terms.الدَّرَنُ: dirt or filth, representing what is removed by washing
key_terms.الذُّنُوبُ: sins, the spiritual impurities erased through salat
key_terms.السَّرِيِّ: a flowing stream, used as a metaphor for continual cleansing
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the recurring act of worship that spiritually purifies
key_terms.النَّهَرُ: a river, clarifying the image of abundant flowing water
key_terms.خَمْسَ مَرَّاتٍ: five times, referring to repeated daily practice
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he washes himself, indicating repeated bodily cleansing

ai.seo_question: How does Imam عليه السلام describe the effect of the five daily prayers on sins?
ai.summary: This hadith compares the five daily salat to repeated washing in a river that removes dirt from the body. In the same way, regular salat purifies a person from sins and shows the spiritual cleansing power and ongoing importance of daily worship.
